text: Net revenue increased 9% to $4.8 billion, driven by higher volumes and a full year of the acquired distribution business.
Net revenue increased 14% to $11.3 billion, driven by higher volumes in the oncology portfolio and new indications.
Net revenue decreased 11% to $6.1 billion, as lower realized prices more than offset higher volumes.
Gross margin declined 140 basis points to 31.2% as freight and packaging costs rose faster than pricing.
Gross margin improved 90 basis points to 76.5% on a favorable mix and lower royalty costs.
Gross margin declined 310 basis points to 38.4% as unit operating costs rose while prices fell.
Operating expenses rose 6% on higher wages and integration costs for acquired warehouses.
Operating expenses rose 18% on higher research spending for three late-stage programs.
Operating expenses rose 4% on higher maintenance and contractor costs in the field.
We ended the year with $620 million of cash and an undrawn $1.0 billion revolving credit facility.
We ended the year with $5.4 billion of cash and an undrawn $2.5 billion revolving credit facility.
We ended the year with $1.3 billion of cash and an undrawn $3.0 billion revolving credit facility.
Total debt was $2.1 billion, including $1.5 billion of senior notes at a weighted average rate of 4.1%.
Total debt was $8.2 billion, including $3.0 billion of new senior notes issued to fund an acquisition.
Total debt was $4.6 billion, and net debt to EBITDAX ended the year at 0.9 times.
The board raised the quarterly dividend 7% to $0.46 per share and repurchased 2.3 million shares.
The board raised the quarterly dividend 5% to $0.84 per share and repurchased 4.1 million shares.
The board kept the quarterly base dividend at $0.30 per share and repurchased 9.8 million shares.
A large share of our sales comes from three customers; the loss of any of them would materially reduce revenue.
A large share of our sales comes from one product whose patent expires in 2027; generic entry would materially reduce revenue.
A large share of our sales comes from one basin; disruption there would materially reduce revenue.
For next year we expect revenue growth of 4% to 6% and a modest recovery in gross margin.
For next year we expect revenue growth of 8% to 10% and stable gross margin.
For next year we expect revenue to be flat to down 3% and production growth of 2%.
